title: Stream lane mapping, SSE backpressure hints, and function-call consistency
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Goal: implement a lane-aware SSE framing model with explicit backpressure hints and deterministic function-call boundaries that survive reconnects and partial replay. Background: current SSE implementation sometimes delivers function-call JSON fragments out of order or duplicated after a reconnect. This ticket defines a lightweight per-subscription lane mapping, chunk provenance metadata, and a small set of headers/fields to allow clients and SDKs to: (1) apply backpressure signals from server, (2) resume exactly at lane offsets, and (3) rehydrate function-call frames atomically without relying on large buffer windows.
acceptance_criteria: Server emits X-RW-Lane and X-RW-Offset headers on initial SSE handshake and for periodic heartbeats
Each stream chunk carries a small provenance tuple (lane_id, offset, chunk_id) in the event envelope
Clients can reconnect and resume by supplying last_seen_lane_offsets in Resume-Token header and receive deltas only for lanes that advanced
Function-call frames are annotated with a fence boolean and a stable call_id; clients never process partial function-call payloads even if fragments arrive across reconnects
Backpressure hints are exposed via X-RW-Backpressure header with values: none | advisory | required and SDK adapts batching accordingly
Compatibility shim supports legacy JSONL streaming: server can emit legacy-compatible events when Accept: application/jsonl is negotiated
E2E tests show <=1% duplicate function-call deliveries during reconnect scenarios and no client-visible partial function-call objects
design_notes: Use lane model: each logical output stream gets assigned a lane_id on subscription. Lanes are cheap (16-bit) and allow independent offsets for KV-cache-able prefixes.
Chunk envelope: add a top-level 'rw_meta' object in SSE data payload with lane_id, offset, seq, and boundary_hint. Keep payload small to avoid overhead.
Function-call atomicity: fragments marked with fence=true indicate final fragment; function-call not emitted to client until fence observed. call_id deterministic per-call to dedupe on reconnect.
Resume tokens: server issues compact resume tokens that are a concatenation of lane_id:offset pairs (base64-encoded). Clients present Resume-Token header on reconnect.
Backpressure: server computes simple score (queue_depth / capacity) and maps to none/advisory/required. SDKs use advisory to increase batching, required to throttle client send rate.
Compatibility: for legacy clients, the server will flatten rw_meta into top-level fields and set Content-Type to application/jsonl when negotiated. Document the shim in SDK changelog.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (server): implement lane assignment + offset bookkeeping and emit headers on subscription (2d)
Phase 2 (server): attach rw_meta envelope to each chunk and implement compact resume token generation (3d)
Phase 3 (server): function-call fencing + call_id generation + dedupe on reconnect (3d)
Phase 4 (sdk): consume lane headers, maintain last_seen_lane_offsets, and implement reconnect flow using Resume-Token (4d)
Phase 5 (compat): add Accept negotiation for legacy JSONL and test with old SDKs (2d)
Phase 6 (tests/observability): add unit + integration tests and Console dashboards for per-lane throughput/backpressure (2d)
testing_plan: Unit tests for resume token encoding/decoding and lane offset arithmetic
Integration test simulating client reconnects at random offsets with duplicated fragments; assert function-call atomicity and <1% duplicates
Chaos test injecting partial fragment loss and network reorders; verify client SDK reconstructs sequence and emits event order per-lane
Load test to measure overhead of rw_meta envelope at 20k concurrent streams; ensure <3% token/latency overhead
Compatibility tests: legacy client negotiation receives application/jsonl and can parse flattened events
rollout_plan: Beta: enable for 10% of hosted streams behind feature flag; gather telemetry for duplicate function-call occurrences and backpressure tripping
Gradual ramp: 25% -> 50% -> 100% over two weeks if metrics stable
SDK releases: patch for node/python to handle Resume-Token and fencing prior to 25% ramp
Monitor: add console alerts for lane gap anomalies and resume token mismatches
